specPoints.text: understand the biological consequences of pollution of air by sulfur dioxide and carbon monoxide

primer.text: Air pollution harms living things through two named gases. This note shows how carbon monoxide hijacks haemoglobin and starves the blood of oxygen, and how sulfur dioxide turns into acid rain that damages plants, aquatic life, soil and human breathing.

lessons.title: Polluted Air, Damaged Life
lessons.opening: Two pollutant gases carry most of the biological damage on this syllabus: carbon monoxide grips haemoglobin and starves the blood of oxygen, while sulfur dioxide dissolves into rain to form acid rain that scalds plants, aquatic life and soil.
keyPoints: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin, reducing oxygen transport in the blood.
High carbon monoxide concentrations can lead to suffocation and death.
Sulfur dioxide combines with water vapour in the atmosphere to form acid rain.
Acid rain damages plants, aquatic life and soil, and sulfur dioxide causes respiratory problems in humans.

low.restatement: One gas steals the seats on blood cells; the other turns rain acidic and burns the living world.
low.analogy: A bus where an impostor occupies every passenger seat, and acid fog corroding everything it settles on.
low.examPointer: Keep the two gases separate: carbon monoxide attacks blood, sulfur dioxide attacks through acid rain.

medium.restatement: The damage is chemical in both cases: carbon monoxide outcompetes oxygen for haemoglobin sites, so the blood carries less oxygen and high doses suffocate; sulfur dioxide reacts with atmospheric water vapour, and the acid rain that forms erodes plant surfaces, acidifies soils and waters, and irritates airways.
medium.analogy: One thief steals the delivery van itself, while the other poisons the roads the van must drive on.
medium.examPointer: For suffocation questions, name the haemoglobin blocking; for environmental questions, name acid rain formation.

check.stem: Which blood component does carbon monoxide bind to?

options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
Carbon monoxide targets the oxygen carrier, not immune cells.
Platelets clot blood; they do not carry oxygen.
Plasma carries dissolved food, but carbon monoxide ignores it.

check.stem: Why does carbon monoxide poisoning suffocate the body?

options.text: Because haemoglobin bound to carbon monoxide cannot carry oxygen
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.

options.text: Because the lungs fill with fluid
options.explanation: Fluid in the lungs is not the mechanism.
Cells do not burst; their oxygen seats are simply occupied.
Swelling is not how carbon monoxide acts.

check.stem: How does sulfur dioxide produce acid rain?

options.text: It combines with water vapour in the atmosphere to form acidic rain
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.

options.text: It burns forests directly with heat
options.explanation: The gas acts through rain chemistry, not direct heat.

options.text: It freezes into acid snow at ground level
options.explanation: The combination happens with water vapour in the air.
Cave chemistry is not the acid rain route.

check.stem: Which system of the human body suffers from sulfur dioxide exposure?

options.text: The respiratory system, causing breathing problems
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.
Bones are not the target of sulfur dioxide.

options.text: The digestive system, ulcerating the gut
options.explanation: The gut is not the documented target here.
Respiration is the affected system.

check.stem: A lake loses its fish after acidic rain falls on its catchment. Which pollutant caused it?

options.text: Sulfur dioxide, through the acid rain it formed
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.
Carbon monoxide poisons blood, not lake water chemistry.
Methane drives warming, not lake acidification.
Nitrogen gas is inert and harmless here.

check.stem: State the biological effect of carbon monoxide on oxygen transport.
check.modelAnswer: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin, reducing the transport of oxygen in the blood.

check.stem: Name the kind of rain produced when sulfur dioxide combines with water vapour.
check.modelAnswer: Sulfur dioxide combines with water vapour to form acid rain.

check.stem: Explain why high carbon monoxide concentrations can be fatal.
check.modelAnswer: High concentrations can be fatal because most haemoglobin becomes blocked, so the blood cannot deliver enough oxygen and the body suffocates.

check.stem: A city reports both traffic smog and coal-burning haze. Match each hazard.
check.modelAnswer: Traffic smog brings carbon monoxide, which blocks haemoglobin, while coal haze brings sulfur dioxide, which forms acid rain and irritates breathing.

glossary.definition: A poisonous gas that binds to haemoglobin and blocks oxygen transport in blood.
The pigment in red blood cells that normally carries oxygen around the body.
A pollutant gas that combines with water vapour in the atmosphere to form acid rain.
Rain made acidic by dissolved pollutant gases, damaging plants, aquatic life and soil.
